recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Do not narrow Timing.repeat.bounds[x] or add redundant prose for FHIR-5951; future work on expressing simultaneous start date and uncertain duration/range should follow the later extension-path decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-5951 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core datatypes change request asking that Timing allow an overall duration without tying the timing to a specific date by changing Timing.repeat.bounds to a choice element and updating the definition.
initial_application: The seed was explicitly applied in SVN revision 5605, now git commit fca58ccc39dd07aaf03838155eb8654a5f713d9c, which changed source/datatypes/timing.xml from Timing.repeat.bounds with type Period to Timing.repeat.bounds[x] with type Duration | Period and updated the description. The closely related FHIR-6252 application in commit 2fbb4392eeaedcf258c8e4f38bbe77af755cb2d6 then added Range and clarified the definition.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Timing as an active datatype and marks it normative. The current authoritative Timing spreadsheet defines Timing.repeat.bounds[x] as Duration | Range | Period and describes a duration, range of possible length, or Period start/end bounds. FHIR-8344 was resolved as done under another task because bounds[x] already had duration support, and FHIR-31559 chose an extension approach for combined start-date plus duration/range expression instead of changing the base bounds choice.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope source already conveys the seed issue's required semantics, and the type list should remain broader than the seed's original wording because later published/applied work intentionally added Range.

related_jiras.note: Published follow-up on the same Timing.repeat.bounds[x] element that added Range to support duration ranges.

Later Timing duration/range plus start-date issue that chose an extension approach rather than changing the base bounds[x] choice.
